newsitem.title: TURKEY: Libya to pay debts to Turks - leading contractor.
newsitem.headline: Libya to pay debts to Turks - leading contractor.

text.p: Tripoli has ordered the partial payment of more than $300 million of unpaid debts to Turkish contractors, a leading contractor said on Wednesday.
Barlas Turan, head of the Association of Turkish Contractors in Libya, said Tripoli owed the group's members $348 million.
"The legal procedures are complete concerning $188 million of this amount and this is in a position to be paid now," he told Reuters in Ankara.

Turkey's Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan last week returned from a visit to Libya, during which Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi severely criticised Turkey's treatment of the Kurds and accused it of being a Western stooge.
Erbakan faced criticism from the West for supporting Libya against Western charges that Tripoli backs terrorism and was harshly rebuked at home.

Few foreign leaders have visited Libya since the United Nations slapped a limited embargo on Tripoli in 1991 for its refusal to hand over two Libyans suspected of blowing up a Pan Am airliner in Scotland in 1988.
But Turkish contractors say they wish to stay in the big Libyan market despite the political problems and the debts.
During Erbakan's visit the two sides agreed on the initial payment of $120 million, due in 1994 but never paid.
Turan said $60 million of this amount would be paid immediately -- up from the $40 million agreed during Erbakan's visit -- and the rest in installments of $4 million.
Another $68 million could be paid locally, he said.
Turan did not say how the rest of the money would be paid.
Turkish contractors began work in Libya in the early 1970s and have undertaken giant construction projects worth a total of $8.6 billion since then.
